title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows & Risk Exceptions
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's authoritative security and compliance practices for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC requirements, incident response (security-focused), compliance evidence collection workflows, and risk/exception management. It is intended for engineers, SREs, security reviewers, and compliance owners.

Scope
- Applies to: all Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated control plane components, and Private deployment reference artifacts where Redwood provides operational or delivery guidance.
- Excludes: customer-managed application code unless Redwood is providing private deployment installation support (see related private-deployment runbooks).

Owner & Key Contacts
- Policy owner: Security Engineering (owner: Aisha Patel, security@redwood.example.com)
- Audit pipeline owner: Observability Platform (owner: Marcus Lee)
- Evidence workflows: Compliance & GRC (owner: Elena Gomez)
- PagerDuty: sec-oncall (PGD ID: PRD_SEC_1)

Principles
1. Least privilege by default: roles grant minimal rights to perform tasks; temporary elevation is audited.
2. Centralized authentication with strong MFA and federated SSO (OIDC / SAML).
3. All security-relevant activity is captured end-to-end in the audit pipeline and stored according to retention policy.
4. Exceptions are time-boxed, documented, and risk-reviewed.

1) RBAC & Authentication
Overview
- Primary identity provider: Redwood SSO (SAML/OIDC) backed by the corporate IdP (Okta).
- Service-to-service identity: short-lived mTLS certs issued by internal CA (cert-manager), or workload identities in cloud providers (IAM roles).
- RBAC implemented via the rbac-service and policy-engine (open-policy-agent / OPA).

Role model (high level)
- developer: read/write limited dev resources (dev clusters, feature flags), no production access.
- platform-engineer: infra runbooks, CI/CD pipelines, limited prod ops permissions.
- sre: production monitoring and incident controls (read/write to production metrics, runbooks).
- security: full audit read access, access to incident evidence stores.
- admin: emergency, break-glass; requires two-person approval and an access justification ticket.

Provisioning and lifecycle
1. All role assignments must be created via identity-management workflows (ui or rbacctl CLI).
2. Access reviews: quarterly automated reviews for critical roles (admin, security, sre).
3. Temporary elevation: use Access Requests (1-8 hour windows) logged by the rbac-service and require approver from the owner_team.

Example policy table
| Role | Allowed scopes | Approval requirement |
|---|---|---|
| developer | dev-cluster:read, logs:read | team lead auto-approve |
| sre | prod-metrics:read, prod-ops:write | 1 approver from SRE lead |
| admin | all:control-plane | 2-person approval + ticket |

Enforcement points
- API gateway: enforces JWT claims and scopes.
- rbac-service: policy decision point (PDP) using OPA; cached decisions at edge proxies with TTL 60s.
- Datastore-level: DB roles limited by service account.

CLI examples
- Grant a role: rbacctl grant --principal user:eli --role sre --expires 2028-04-01
- Request temporary access: rbacctl request --role admin --duration 4h --reason "incident triage"

2) Audit Logging
What we log
- Authentication events (login, refresh, SSO assertion).
- Authorization decisions (allow/deny) with policy version id and input context.
- Admin actions: role grants, secrets rotation, config changes.
- Data access to sensitive datasets (read/write) with dataset id and query fingerprint.
- System-level events: image deploys, autoscaler decisions, kernel upgrades for serving runtime.

Pipeline architecture
- Sources: application logs (structured JSON), system audit agents (auditd), cloud-provider audit streams (CloudTrail / GCP CloudAudit).
- Aggregation: audit-collector (Fluentd/Vector) -> Kafka topic: redwood.audit.events -> processing zone (filtering & enrichment) -> long-term store (Splunk for 90 days hot, GCS cold archives).

Audit schema (example)
{
  "timestamp": "2028-03-04T12:01:23Z",
  "service": "auth-service",
  "event": "authorization_decision",
  "principal": "user:eli@redwood.example.com",
  "resource": "project:prod/dataset:customer-secrets",
  "action": "read",
  "decision": "deny",
  "policy_id": "rbac-policy-v3.2.1",
  "request_id": "abcd-1234-efgh-5678"
}

Retention and SLOs
- Critical audit events (authN/authZ, admin actions): kept hot for 90 days in Splunk with 99.9% availability SLO. Archived to cold storage (encrypted GCS) for 7 years for compliance.
- Non-critical telemetry: 365 days in cold storage.
- Audit processing lag: 95th percentile < 2 minutes from event generation to indexed/queriable state. Owner: Observability Platform.

Access to audit logs
- Role-based: security and compliance teams have read access; admins require just-in-time approval. All access generates additional audit events.

3) Data Residency & Retention
Residency controls
- Customer data tiering: sensitive PII and regulated datasets are tagged with residency policies at ingestion.
- Hosted control plane: data for customers selecting region EU-1 remains in eu-1 by default.
- Dedicated & Private: follow customer-managed region choices; Redwood packaging enforces region-local evidence stores where requested.

Retention matrix
| Data type | Hot retention | Cold archive | Encryption |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| AuthN/AuthZ events | 90 days | 7 years | AES-256 (KMS: redwood-kms) |
| Model logs (non-PII) | 30 days | 365 days | AES-256 |
| Customer PII | 90 days | per-contract (min 1 year) | Customer KMS optional |

Data deletion and proof-of-deletion
1. Deletion requests originate from product or legal and must include a deletion ticket (JIRA) with dataset id and retention justification.
2. Runbook: verify snapshotting, execute secure-delete (cloud provider purge + object lifecycle verification), and record deletion proof (sha256 manifest) in evidence store.
3. For regulated requests, provide attestation letter signed by Compliance.

4) Secure SDLC Requirements
Gate criteria (applies to all code affecting production or customer data):
- Mandatory automated unit + integration tests with >= 80% pass on pipeline.
- SCA and dependency vulnerability gating: no critical/high untriaged CVEs allowed.
- Static analysis and secrets scanning (pre-merge): no secrets in diffs.
- Architecture review for infra changes impacting network boundaries or data residency.

Review & approvals
- PR approvals: 1 peer for minor, 2 for infra or security-impacting changes.
- Security review: required for any change touching authentication, RBAC, audit pipeline, or evidence workflows.

CI/CD hygiene
- Pipelines run with ephemeral runner identities; artifacts signed by build-service (artifact-signer).
- Immutable deployment artifacts: images pushed with content-addressable tags.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures
Detection & Triage
- Alerts: generated by the detection pipeline (IDS, anomaly detectors in observability, WAF). PagerDuty sec-oncall is primary.
- Initial triage owner: on-call SRE + Security lead.

Containment & Eradication (high-level steps)
1. Triage and categorize (CONFIDENTIALITY / INTEGRITY / AVAILABILITY impact).
2. If credential compromise suspected: rotate affected service principals, revoke tokens, rotate KMS keys where impacted.
3. Preserve evidence: take forensic snapshots, detach volumes as read-only, copy audit logs to evidence-bucket (see Evidence Workflows).
4. Patch and redeploy with mitigations.

Forensics & evidence handling checklist
- Capture live memory only after approval from Security Incident Lead.
- Collect kernel and runtime logs, audit stream slices (t0-24h), and associated network flow captures.
- Hash all artifacts (sha256) and store in evidence-bucket with metadata: incident_id, collector, timestamp.

Post-incident
- Postmortem must be completed within 7 days (public summary for product teams, full write-up for leadership and compliance).
- Root-cause analysis and remediation plan tracked as a JIRA EPIC.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Automated evidence generation
- Controls-as-code: CI jobs generate attestations for pipeline controls (e.g., automated proof that secret scanning ran on every PR). Artifacts are saved to evidence-bucket: gs://redwood-evidence/<control>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<artifact>.json

Manual evidence collection
- For policy or legal requests, Compliance owner opens an evidence collection ticket; workflow: identify control IDs -> export artifacts -> run evidence-collector tool -> upload to evidence-bucket -> create audit package (signed manifest).

Evidence retention & access
- Evidence artifacts follow the control retention schedule (typically 7 years). Access is limited to Compliance, Audit, and delegated reviewers. All downloads are logged.

Example commands
- Copy artifact to evidence bucket: aws s3 cp ./attestation.json s3://redwood-evidence/controls/rbac/2028-03-04/ --sse aws:kms
- Generate a control report: evidencectl generate --control rbac.access-review --since 2028-01-01 --out rbac-report-2028-03-04.json

7) Risk & Exceptions
Exception request process
1. Submit exception: security-exceptions@redwood.example.com with template fields (service, control-id, risk-description, compensating-controls, duration requested).
2. Security Risk Review Board evaluates within 5 business days.
3. If approved: assign mitigation owners, monitoring SLOs, and an automatic expiry (max 90 days).
4. Renewal: must provide new justification and evidence.

Exception template (required fields)
- service
- control_id
- justification
- compensating_controls
- estimated_risk_level (low/medium/high)
- owner and approver

Metrics & reporting
- Weekly exceptions digest published to leadership with counts by severity.
- Quarterly risk posture review with exec summary.
